questions.question: Does CFCs causes skin burn? Directly answer 'yes' or 'no'.
questions.v2_correction_reason: defective_question: The deck never states that CFCs cause skin burn. It attributes burning to UV radiation: p20 ('P1h: UV Radiation on People') says 'UV radiation can damage cells in our skin', 'before burning' and 'You get the burn time from the radiation'. CFCs appear only on p21 ('P1h: UV Radiation on Earth and Atmosphere'), where their stated effect is on the ozone layer: 'The ozone is thinning though by CFCs'. Separately, benchmark_evidence_pages cites p18, which is 'P1g: Receiving Signals' and mentions neither CFCs nor skin; the CFC slide is p21. QUESTION REWRITTEN IN V2: adding 'directly' removes the ambiguity that made the original arguable in both directions. The deck supports a causal chain -- CFCs thin the ozone layer (p21), a thinner layer lets more UV through, and UV burns skin (p20) -- so 'does CFCs cause skin burn' is defensible as yes via that chain and as no on the direct reading. Asking whether CFCs DIRECTLY cause skin burn is determinate from the same two pages: the deck attributes burning to UV radiation and gives CFCs' only stated effect as ozone thinning, so the answer is no. This also matches how the corpus treats the neighbouring qknorm pair -- llama-1 is discussed and its property can be refuted ('no'), while llama-3 never appears ('Not answerable') -- here both CFCs and skin burning are discussed, so the item belongs in the refutable class.
questions.v2_question: Does CFCs directly cause skin burn? Answer 'yes' or 'no'.

What plants is on the cover of each chapter?
questions.v2_correction_reason: incomplete_answer: Answer key widened to accept the empty-set form of the same refusal. The page the question names exists and the thing it asks about is verifiably absent from it, so reporting 'none' -- or, for a how-many, the count 0 -- says exactly what 'Not answerable' means here. Widening removes a fragile edge without deleting the negative sample: a system that names an item, or invents a value, still fails. The chapter opener carries a full-width leopard photograph and no plants; the twin question, 'what animal is on the cover of each chapter', is answered leopard. The absence is verifiable from the rendered slide rather than merely unstated. NOT applied where the container itself is missing (page ranges outside the document such as Pages 200-205 or 400-640, and '2311.16502v3.pdf' Figure 10, which has no caption anywhere in the paper), where the question names an entity the document never covers (Beijing in a Nepal media survey, a microwave in a dishwasher manual, TRUCS level-6, survey years 2018 and 2022), where it asks for the complement of a set against an unbounded universe ('mi_phone.pdf', signal icons not in the Status Bar), or where the set is short rather than empty (the same EarthLink deck asks for 'another TWO companies' when exactly one further contact carries a phone number). In those cases 'none' is an over-claim rather than a reading of the document.

questions.v2_correction_reason: incomplete_answer: Answer key widened to accept the empty-set form of the same refusal. The page the question names exists and the thing it asks about is verifiably absent from it, so reporting 'none' -- or, for a how-many, the count 0 -- says exactly what 'Not answerable' means here. Widening removes a fragile edge without deleting the negative sample: a system that names an item, or invents a value, still fails. PDF p. 10 of this 17-page CQC inspection report carries no embedded images at all -- it is the prose 'Our findings' page -- so the count of red logos on it is zero. NOT applied where the container itself is missing (page ranges outside the document such as Pages 200-205 or 400-640, and '2311.16502v3.pdf' Figure 10, which has no caption anywhere in the paper), where the question names an entity the document never covers (Beijing in a Nepal media survey, a microwave in a dishwasher manual, TRUCS level-6, survey years 2018 and 2022), where it asks for the complement of a set against an unbounded universe ('mi_phone.pdf', signal icons not in the Status Bar), or where the set is short rather than empty (the same EarthLink deck asks for 'another TWO companies' when exactly one further contact carries a phone number). In those cases 'none' is an over-claim rather than a reading of the document.
